text: The program is built, presented, and adopted. Now it has to survive without you in the room. This video writes the three documents that make that possible.
Two glossary entries answer what each term means. An ownership matrix answers who to call. A checklist answers what the Oracle incident actually raised: did we register what's really there.
Active Customer and Engaged Account each state their exclusions plainly -- Oracle's signal and Salesforce's signal don't substitute for each other -- so neither can be quietly reinterpreted later.
The checklist is written against what actually happened: diff a source's real schema against Purview's list, flag hidden base tables, and give every provisional result a named owner and date.
Three documents, stored where the next person will find them. Last video: an honest look at what this program changed, and what isn't finished.
